blocks.text: Function Declarations

Earlier in this tutorial, you learned that functions are declared with the
following syntax:
A function declaration uses the function keyword and a function name.
function myFunction(a, b) {return a * b}
blocks.caption: Examples
Examples

blocks.text:
Declared functions are not executed immediately. They are "saved for later use",
and will be executed later, when they are invoked (called upon).
You can call a function before or after it is declared in the code.

blocks.caption: Examples
Examples

blocks.text: Function Expressions
A function expression stores a function inside a variable.
The function can be anonymous (without a name).
Function expressions are executed only when the code reaches them.
const x = function (a, b) {return a * b};
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
After a function expression has been stored in a variable, the variable can
be used as a function:

const x = function (a, b) {return a * b};

let z = x(4, 3);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Hoisting
Function declarations are hoisted to the top of their scope.
Function expressions are not hoisted in the same way.
Function declarations can be called before they are defined.
Function expressions can not be called before they are defined.

const sum = add(2, 3); // Will work

function add(a, b) {return a + b;}
blocks.caption: Examples

blocks.text:
const sum = add(2, 3); // ⛔ Will generate error

const add = function (a, b) {return a + b;};
blocks.caption: Examples

blocks.text: Key Differences

rows:
Syntax:
A statement starting with the function keyword, followed by a required name.

Syntax:
A part of an expression or assignment, and can be anonymous (without a name).

Hoisting:
The function is moved to the top of its scope before code execution,
allowing you to call it from anywhere within that code scope, even before its definition.

Hoisting:
The variable holding the function might be hoisted
(depending on var, let, or const), but the function assignment itself is not.
You can only call it after it has been defined in the code scope.

Flexibility:
Primarily used for general-purpose functions that need to be available globally or in a specific scope.

Flexibility:
Can be used in various contexts, such as arguments to other
functions (callbacks), immediately invoked function expressions, and assigned to object properties.

blocks.text: The Function() Constructor
Functions can also be defined with the JavaScript Function() constructor, but this is rarely used.

const myFunction = new Function("a", "b", "return a * b");

let x = myFunction(4, 3);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: You actually don't have to use the function constructor. The example above is the same as writing:

const myFunction = function (a, b) {return a * b};

let x = myFunction(4, 3);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Most of the time, you can avoid using the new keyword in JavaScript.
